_about: Keyword (matched through core.fuzzy, typo tolerant) -> lines about that kind of object.
_phase: seed-v0 (#1002 attachment 1) + supplement additions (#1002 supplement via #1017 batch 2)
_license: Original to Print Handy; MIT with the project.

benchy.text: Ah, {title} — the little boat that judges every printer and finds most of them merely adequate.
{title} has docked at last, ready to be photographed from exactly one flattering angle.
Every printer must face {title} eventually, like a tiny floating exam with a smokestack.

box.text: {title} is a container with big dreams, mostly involving containing slightly smaller containers.
A fresh {title} joins the eternal quest to put things inside other things, neatly.
{title} is empty right now, but give it a week and it will contain pure mystery.

bracket.text: {title} is here to hold things up, emotionally unavailable but structurally extremely supportive.
Nobody celebrates {title} at parties, yet everything it holds would fall apart without it.
{title}: the unsung hero whose entire personality is two holes and quiet reliability.

dragon.text: {title} has hatched, and it is already acting like it owns the treasure and the shelf.
Behold {title}, a fearsome dragon whose main power is looking cool next to dice.
{title} arrived with wings, attitude, and absolutely no plans to guard anything but the desk.

gear.text: {title} is ready to mesh, spin, and take credit for the whole machine working.
One more {title} for the collection, because a single gear is just a round decoration.
{title} has teeth, purpose, and strong opinions about meshing with its neighbors.

helmet.text: {title} is complete, sized for a hero, a costume, or a very confident houseplant.
Behold {title}, protection for a head that has clearly made some ambitious plans.
{title} looks ready for battle, provided the battle is indoors and mostly posing.

hook.text: {title} is small, curved, and about to carry far more responsibility than it signed up for.
Behold {title}, the tiny wall hero that will hold keys, coats, and household chaos.
{title} will spend its life hanging around, which is either lazy or literally the job.

mask.text: {title} is ready for a mysterious entrance at a party nobody has planned yet.
With {title} complete, someone can now look dramatic while remaining completely anonymous at the store.
{title}: instant intrigue, zero actual secrets, and a very committed eye-hole game.

organizer.text: {title} promises this is the year the desk finally stays tidy for a full week.
Behold {title}, a tiny city planner for pens, cables, and good intentions.
{title} will organize everything perfectly, right up until someone opens a drawer nearby.

phone stand.text: {title} is ready to hold a phone at the perfect angle for ignoring notifications comfortably.
With {title} on duty, the phone finally has a throne worthy of its screen time.
{title} exists so a phone can recline like royalty while its owner does actual work.

planter.text: {title} is ready for a plant that will either thrive or be dramatically replaced monthly.
A new home for greenery: {title}, now accepting one plant and unlimited optimism.
{title} gives a houseplant the fancy apartment it has been manifesting all spring.

skull.text: {title} has emerged, spooky on the outside and completely hollow where it counts.
Behold {title}, the only skull in the house that improves with shelf lighting.
{title} looks like it has ancient secrets, but it mostly just holds pens now.

star.text: {title} has arrived, five points of pure confidence and zero plans to twinkle responsibly.
Behold {title}, a celebrity among shapes, ready for its close-up on the highest shelf.
{title} proves that being pointy in five directions is a complete personality.

sword.text: {title} has been forged, more or less, in the ancient fires of a warm nozzle.
With {title} complete, someone is now legally required to make swooshing noises while holding it.
{title}: all the drama of a legendary blade, none of the sharpening responsibilities.

toy.text: {title} is officially too cute to be called a test print, whatever anyone says.
A wild {title} appears, and productivity in the room drops by a measurable amount.
{title} was made for play, but it will mostly supervise from the shelf, judging quietly.

vase.text: {title} is ready to hold flowers, water, and the secret that it is mostly decorative confidence.
A new {title} enters the home, immediately promoted to chief dust collector with excellent curves.
{title} proves once again that a container with no lid can still contain unlimited style.

clip.text: {title} has one job: hold together everything except the printer budget.
{title} is tiny, useful, and already bracing for an unreasonable workload.
{title} holds the line, the cables, and the whole operation together, barely.

cable.text: {title} promises tidy wiring, which is adorable given the rest of this desk.
{title} attempts diplomacy between cables that have spent years fighting.
{title} has brought order to exactly one cable; the rest remain at large.

mount.text: {title} exists because buying a bracket would have been insufficiently complicated.
{title} looks sturdy enough to support an alarming amount of misplaced confidence.
{title} is now load-bearing, emotionally if not structurally.

enclosure.text: {title} gives an object its own tiny house before you finish yours.
{title} made a respectable shelter for something that probably doesn't pay rent.
{title} is a tiny house that will somehow end up storing screws.

holder.text: {title} is a dedicated parking space for an object that kept escaping.
{title} exists to hold one thing while the rest of the room stays chaotic.
{title} reports for duty, holding the one thing it was born to hold.

hinge.text: {title} introduces moving parts into a hobby already rich in surprises.
{title} bends the rules of what should have been a simple connection.
{title} swings between genius and liability, smoothly and repeatedly.

jig.text: {title} is a tool for making the next tool slightly less embarrassing.
{title} makes repetitive work precise, unlike the decision to print it at midnight.
{title} ensures the next mistake happens in exactly the same place every time.

drawer.text: {title} offers the comforting illusion that the desk is now organized.
{title} is where small things go to become officially missing.
{title} slides open to reveal the thing you needed last week.

adapter.text: {title} is a peace treaty between two objects that refuse to cooperate.
{title} solves a compatibility problem that capitalism kindly manufactured.
{title} lets two stubborn objects finally shake hands.

rack.text: {title} takes one more step toward making the server closet look intentional.
{title} is proof even a homelab can benefit from pretending to be organized.
{title} is one slot closer to a setup that actually looks planned.

keychain.text: {title} gives a keyring the weight and drama of a museum exhibit.
{title} will be impossible to find precisely when the keys are needed.
{title} makes the keys heavier, fancier, and somehow easier to lose.
